result.stdout:
Description:
  Demeanor for .NET v6 - Code Obfuscator

Usage:
  demeanor <assembly> [command] [options]

Arguments:
  <assembly>  Path to the .NET assembly to obfuscate.

Options:
  --out, --output-dir <out>            Output directory for the obfuscated assembly.
  --include-publics                    Also obfuscate public/protected symbols. Without this flag, publicly visible types and members in library DLLs are preserved. Use for executables that are not referenced by other assemblies.
  --include-deps                       Also obfuscate co-located private dependency assemblies (transitive closure). System and third-party assemblies are loaded for reference only.
  --names <names>                      Name generation mode: Alpha (a,b,c) or Unicode (Canadian Aboriginal Syllabics - most systems lack the font). [default: Alpha]
  --prefix <prefix>                    Namespace prefix for obfuscated top-level types.
  --no-aggressive                      Disable aggressive renaming. By default (Enterprise), all renamed members share the same obfuscated name and property/event metadata is stripped.
  --no-strings                         Disable string encryption.
  --no-constants                       Disable integer constant encryption.
  --no-resources                       Disable encryption of embedded resources.
  --no-virtual-rename                  Disable MethodImpl-based virtual override renaming (Enterprise). When enabled, overrides of external methods like ToString and interface implementations are renamed.
  --no-enum-deletion                   Disable deletion of enum member fields (Enterprise). When enabled, all static literal fields on renamed enums are removed.
  --no-anti-debug                      Disable anti-debug detection (Enterprise). When enabled, debugger detection checks are scattered across method entry points.
  --no-anti-tamper                     Disable anti-tamper integrity verification (Enterprise). When enabled, a module initializer verifies the assembly file
[truncated]

  Wire automatic Release-build obfuscation into a .csproj in the current directory.

Usage:
  demeanor <assembly> init [<assembly>] [options]

Arguments:
  <assembly>  Path to the .NET assembly to obfuscate.
  <assembly>  Optional path to a Release build assembly. If supplied, runs an audit and prints suggested exclusions before writing MSBuild integration.

Options:
  --project <project>  Path to the .csproj to wire. Skips the single-directory discovery pass entirely.
  --dry-run            Print the MSBuild snippet that would be added, but do not modify any files.
  -?, -h, --help       Show help and usage information
